notes.note: All 'specific places' tests (clause 16.1.4) use a value-returning function called in an alt guard as the specific place; other specific places (templates in receive, altstep local initialisations) are not covered.

Empty table cell read as prohibition. Titan accepts: it does not check the clause 16.1.4 / Table 16 restrictions on functions called from alt guards. Same applies to 18_test_050, 053, 056, 059, 062, 065, 068, 071, 074, 077.
The BNF allows ReturnStatement in BehaviourStatements (also used in control); the restriction comes only from Table 16. Titan accepts return in the control part, so the warning is a Titan deviation.
repeat needs an enclosing alt, so the function also contains an alt (itself prohibited in specific places, 18_test_050). An else-only alt keeps out other restricted operations.
interleave needs receiving/timeout events, so the function also uses a timeout operation, which clause 16.1.4 d) also restricts; the violation cannot be isolated.
map between two control-part component variables is used to avoid also referencing system in control (prohibited separately). Unmap test 18_test_075 does the same.
Execution requires a test port adapter for the mapped port; the map/unmap tests (also 18_test_076) observe the effect via checkstate("Mapped").
